description: Dairy whose cooling, hot-water and steam loads were metered for a year; analysed on its mean production day, hour by hour. Today the CO2 refrigeration units heat the hot water and an electric boiler raises the steam.

provenance.data source: Köster, Bengsch, Widell (2025), Int. J. Refrig. 180, 564-571 (CC BY 4.0) and its data, Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.22877098 (CC BY 4.0): metered 2024 heat loads (one-minute) and hourly electric-boiler electricity.
provenance.stream data: measured: mean production day of 2024 (weekdays with more than 1,500 kWh of boiler electricity), hour by hour; CO2 unit 1 (not metered) at 35 kW from 07:00 to 15:00 as the authors assume (Sec. 3). Published figures reproduced in outputs/koster2025_checks.csv
provenance.temperatures: published (Sec. 2): glycol supply -3.5 to -5 °C, process water about 1 °C, hot water from city water 6.5 °C to 65 °C, steam demands 65-100 °C. Cooling loads are taken isothermal at the supply temperature (-3.5 °C, 1 °C): return temperatures are not published, so the source is a lower bound
provenance.dT_shift_K: assumed: 2.5 K for every stream (dTmin 5 K)
provenance.steam demand: measured boiler electricity with a thermal efficiency of about 1 (Sec. 4.4), including its heat losses (the 35.8 kW night baseload)
provenance.eta_lorenz: assumed: 0.5, as the brewery case; the measured CO2 COPs (Table 2) are depressed by a fouled gas cooler (about 20 K approach, Sec. 4.2) and their operating conditions are not published, so they cannot calibrate it
provenance.source_T_C: published glycol supply -3.5 °C, shifted by -2.5 K
provenance.sink levels: published: hot water to 65 °C (the CO2 units today) and the 65-100 °C steam demands (the paper's proposal: a high-temperature heat pump replacing the electric boiler, Sec. 4.4); shifted by +2.5 K
provenance.basis: none: a screening on the mean production day, in kW; no prices for Norway in this repository
provenance.ambient_T_C: published: 2024 mean of August 15.5 °C and December 0.1 °C is not an annual mean; 7 °C assumed for the ambient-source check only

economics.skipped: no annual basis in the case file

cop_ranges.note: COP of each heat pump on four bases: the case's Lorenz efficiency; manufacturer-data fits (Jesper et al. 2021) at lift = sink outlet - source inlet, with their standard deviation; a glide-matched blend (+16 %, Brendel et al. 2024) for sink glides of 25 K or more; the Lorenz model with the efficiencies achieved by IEA HPT Annex 58 closed-cycle demonstration plants (min, median, max). The fits come from small-glide machines, so for a large sink glide they are a pessimistic bound. fit_in_range = False: the point is outside the data behind the fit.

designs.basis: market products, supplier operating points (median) (not computed: CO2 units (hot water): no supplier product has published points covering this unit)

time_slices.note: Time Slice Model (direct heat recovery only) and Time Average Model (storage at any temperature) per cycle; heat pump with hot and cold storage loops after Stampfli et al. (2019).
